content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all seven figure briefs against the disclosure and the single USER passage in the conversation.

input.summary: Full source-fidelity preflight completed: all 22 claims (independent claims 1, 13, 18 and every dependent limitation), all 27 entries of the numeral ledger and every numbered part in the description, all seven figure briefs and the Brief Description of the Drawings, the abstract, summary, field, background and detailed description were traced limitation-by-limitation to affirmative passages in input/disclosure.md and the single USER passage of input/conversation.md (which is the same text, truncated at "The difference between"). input/brief.md was used only for title, applicant/inventor, no-priority, no-government-support, claim-type and preserved-terminology formalities. Substantially the whole ledger traces cleanly: rail/upper face/lower face/longitudinal slot/printed distance marks, the reversible two-screw fence and its downwardly projecting portion, the removable parallel-faced spacer plate and its setback-only effect, two separate guide carriages with anti-rotation keys, cylindrical hardened-metal replaceable drill bushings with through bores registering with the slot, parallel bores perpendicular to the lower face, threaded clamp knobs with shanks passing into clamping shoes below the rail, the two independent pointers whose reading difference is center-to-center spacing, the transverse center index at the midpoint, the shallow V-shaped sight notch in the second end aligned with the index, the polymer-or-metal material list, the no-motor/battery/sensor/network negative limitation, and the full method sequence all rest on exact disclosure sentences. Section-line designations were verified as identical across FIG. 2 (line 3-3 and line 5-5, arrows and repeated designations at both endpoints), the resulting views FIG-3.md and FIG-5.md, and draft/07-drawings.md; every numeral means exactly one part; no drafting note, placeholder, open question, unresolved alternative, or internal comment remains; no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" broadening statement appears in the application text. Seven defects were found and are reported with fixes. One is critical: FIG-7.md verbalizes a runout/end-position statement for the functional longitudinal slot ("stopping short of the second end of the rail 10") that no inventor passage supports; the disclosure says only "A straight longitudinal slot runs through the rail" and never locates either slot end, so this must be deleted from the figure brief. The remaining six are minor internal-consistency and untraced-detail items: claims 1 and 13 attach the disclosed perpendicularity to the downwardly projecting portion while the source and the description attach it to the fence; claim 11 narrows "read directly" to the distance marks alone while the description recites the distance marks, the transverse center index and the sight notch; claim 13 adds "on the upper face" to the transverse center index, a location stated in neither the source nor the description; numeral 32 is cross-referenced to FIG. 1 and relied on in the FIG. 6 paragraph but appears in neither figure's numeral list; FIG. 1 depicts an unidentified "round body of like size" on the second guide carriage that is the disclosed clamp knob 78; and the description asserts a wear mechanism ("whose bore has been enlarged by use") beyond the source's "replaceable wear parts". No claim, numeral, or figure statement was left untraced, and each finding below quotes the candidate wording, the nearest source passage, and a filing-clean automatic fix.

findings.title: FIG. 7 asserts an untraced end position (runout) for the functional longitudinal slot
findings.where: figures/FIG-7.md, paragraph describing the longitudinal slot 16
findings.detail: The figure brief verbalizes where the longitudinal slot terminates relative to the second end of the rail. The slot is a functional opening (the drill bit, the carriage keys, and the clamp shanks all pass through it), so a statement about its end position is substantive geometry and is not saved by the "shown schematically" convention. No inventor passage locates either end of the slot. The disclosure states only that the slot runs through the rail, and the detailed description likewise says only that it "extends along the length of the rail 10" without terminating it. The inference that the slot must stop short of the second end so as not to run into the sight notch is common engineering knowledge, which is not inventor support.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-7.md): "The longitudinal slot 16 is a straight elongated opening running lengthwise along the band, shown schematically, and stopping short of the second end of the rail 10." Nearest source (input/disclosure.md): "A straight longitudinal slot runs through the rail." The disclosure never states where the slot begins or ends; its only statement about the second end is "A shallow V-shaped sight notch is formed in the second end of the rail and aligned with the center index."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-7.md, replace the sentence with: "The longitudinal slot 16 is a straight elongated opening running lengthwise along the band, shown schematically." Delete the clause "and stopping short of the second end of the rail 10" so that no slot end position is verbalized. Make no compensating addition to the description or claims.

findings.title: Claims 1 and 13 attach perpendicularity to the projecting portion; source and description attach it to the fence
findings.where: draft/09-claims.md, claim 1 (fence element) and claim 13 (fixed fence element); compare draft/08-detailed-description.md, fence paragraph
findings.detail: The disclosure and the detailed description both recite that the fence is perpendicular to the rail. Both independent apparatus claims instead recite that the downwardly projecting portion is perpendicular to the rail. Claims and description must use the same relationship for the same feature; as drafted the claims assign the disclosed geometric relationship to a different element than the specification does.
findings.evidence: Candidate claim 1: "the fence having a downwardly projecting portion that extends below the lower face and that is perpendicular to the rail for bearing against the straight edge"; candidate claim 13: "the fixed fence having a downwardly projecting portion that extends below the lower face and that is perpendicular to the rail for bearing against the straight edge". Description: "The fence 30 is perpendicular to the rail 10, so that when the downwardly projecting portion 32 is held against the workpiece edge 92 the rail 10 extends inward across the front face of the workpiece 90." Source: "The fence is perpendicular to the rail, so the rail extends inward across the workpiece when the fence bears against the edge."
findings.fix: In claim 1 amend to: "a fence releasably secured to the first end of the rail by two screws received in two corresponding mounting holes, the fence being perpendicular to the rail and having a downwardly projecting portion that extends below the lower face for bearing against the straight edge, ...". In claim 13 amend correspondingly to: "a fixed fence at the first end of the rail, the fixed fence being perpendicular to the rail and having a downwardly projecting portion that extends below the lower face for bearing against the straight edge, so that the rail extends inward across the front face;".

findings.title: Claim 11 recites that every setting is read from the distance marks, contradicting the description
findings.where: draft/09-claims.md, claim 11; compare draft/08-detailed-description.md, penultimate substantive paragraph
findings.detail: Claim 11 states that every setting of the jig is read directly from the distance marks. The description states that settings are read from three separate features, and the specification elsewhere makes clear that the centerline placement is set by sighting the transverse center index and the sight notch, not by reading the distance marks. The claim as drafted is inconsistent with the description, and the center index and sight notch cannot simply be added to claim 11 because claim 1 does not recite them (no antecedent basis).
findings.evidence: Candidate claim 11: "...and every setting of the drilling jig is made mechanically and read directly from the distance marks." Description: "Every setting is made mechanically and is read directly from the distance marks 18, the transverse center index 24, and the sight notch 26." Source: "The tool has no motor, battery, electronic sensor, or network connection."
findings.fix: Amend claim 11 to read: "11. The drilling jig of claim 1, wherein the drilling jig has no motor, no battery, no electronic sensor, and no network connection, and every setting of the drilling jig is made mechanically." (Delete "and read directly from the distance marks".)

findings.title: Claim 13 locates the transverse center index "on the upper face", a position not in the source or the description
findings.detail: Claim 13 adds a positional limitation placing the transverse center index on the upper face of the rail. The disclosure says only that the rail has the index at its midpoint, and the detailed description likewise says only that the rail has it at its midpoint and that it runs across the rail. Claim 4, reciting the same feature, correctly omits the face. The added location is therefore both untraced and inconsistent with the parallel claim and the description.
findings.evidence: Candidate claim 13: "a transverse center index on the upper face at a midpoint of the rail". Claim 4 (same feature): "wherein the rail has a transverse center index at a midpoint of the rail." Description: "the rail 10 has a transverse center index 24 at its midpoint. The transverse center index 24 is a mark that runs across the rail 10 transverse to the length of the rail 10..." Nearest source: "The rail has a transverse center index at its midpoint." No source passage assigns the index to a particular face.
findings.fix: Amend claim 13 to read: "a transverse center index at a midpoint of the rail, and a shallow V-shaped sight notch formed in the second end of the rail and aligned with the transverse center index, for sighting on the centerline;". (Delete "on the upper face".) Leave FIG-7.md unchanged, since a top plan view necessarily shows the mark on the visible surface and that placement is not verbalized as a relationship in the application text.

findings.title: Numeral 32 is cross-referenced to FIG. 1 and relied on in the FIG. 6 paragraph but is absent from both figure briefs
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md (fence paragraph and FIG. 6 paragraph); figures/FIG-1.md and figures/FIG-6.md numeral lists
findings.detail: The description cites FIG. 1 for the downwardly projecting portion 32 and then, expressly "Referring to FIG. 6", describes which longitudinal side of the rail portion 32 lies on in the first and second fence orientations. Neither FIG-1.md nor FIG-6.md depicts or lists numeral 32, so the text refers the reader to views that do not carry the part it discusses. The part itself is fully supported by the disclosure, so the inconsistency is corrected by labeling it, not by deleting matter.
findings.evidence: Description: "The fence 30 includes a downwardly projecting portion 32 that extends below the lower face 14 and bears against the workpiece edge 92 (see FIG. 1)." and "Referring to FIG. 6, ... In a first orientation, the downwardly projecting portion 32 lies on a first longitudinal side of the rail 10." FIG-1.md numeral list: "10, 30, 50, 58, 62, 70, 90, 92" (no 32), although the brief already shows the fence "hangs down, contacting a workpiece edge 92". FIG-6.md numeral list: "10, 30, 34, 36" (no 32). Source support for the part: "The fence extends downward from the lower face and bears against one straight edge of the workpiece" and "...moves the downwardly projecting part of the fence from one longitudinal side of the rail to the opposite longitudinal side."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-1.md, change "A fence 30 is attached to the left end of the rail 10 and hangs down, contacting a workpiece edge 92" to "A fence 30 is attached to the left end of the rail 10 and has a downwardly projecting portion 32 that extends below the rail 10 and contacts a workpiece edge 92", and add "- 32: downwardly projecting portion" to its numeral list. In figures/FIG-6.md, add the sentence "The fence 30 has a downwardly projecting portion 32 that stands on one longitudinal side of the rail 10." and add "- 32: downwardly projecting portion" to its numeral list.

findings.title: FIG. 1 depicts an unidentified round body on the second guide carriage that is the disclosed clamp knob 78
findings.where: figures/FIG-1.md, second paragraph and numeral list
findings.detail: The brief instructs that a round body of like size stand on the second guide carriage but leaves it unnamed and unnumbered, while the identical element on the first carriage is called out as clamp knob 58. The element is the second carriage's clamp knob, which the disclosure affirmatively provides and which the numeral ledger already assigns numeral 78. An unexplained element in a figure is an avoidable drawing objection and an internal inconsistency with FIG. 3, which labels the same part 78.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-1.md): "The first guide carriage 50 has a clamp knob 58 on top, shown schematically as a plain round body. A round body of like size stands on top of the second guide carriage 70." Numeral ledger: "78 | clamp knob of the second guide carriage". Source: "Each carriage has a threaded clamp knob above the rail."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-1.md, change the second sentence to "A clamp knob 78 of like size stands on top of the second guide carriage 70, shown schematically as a plain round body." and add "- 78: clamp knob of the second guide carriage" to the numeral list for FIG. 1.

findings.title: Description asserts a bushing wear mechanism (bore enlarged by use) that the source does not disclose
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph beginning "The drill bushing 54 and the drill bushing 74 are wear parts."
findings.detail: The disclosure states that the drill bushings are replaceable wear parts made from hardened metal. It does not state how they wear. The candidate specifies bore enlargement as the wear condition that prompts replacement, which is an untraced operating condition supplied from common engineering knowledge rather than from the inventor.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "Each is made of hardened metal and is received in the body of its guide carriage as a separate piece, so that a drill bushing whose bore has been enlarged by use can be withdrawn from the guide carriage and replaced." Nearest source: "The drill bushings are replaceable wear parts and are made from hardened metal." No source passage describes bore enlargement or any other wear mode.
findings.fix: Amend the sentence to: "Each is made of hardened metal and is received in the body of its guide carriage as a separate piece, so that a worn drill bushing can be withdrawn from the guide carriage and replaced." No claim amendment is needed, since claims 9 and 17 already recite only hardened metal, separability, withdrawability, and replaceability.

findings.title: Claims 1 and 13 attach perpendicularity to the projecting portion; source and description attach it to the fence
findings.where: draft/09-claims.md, claim 1 (fence element) and claim 13 (fixed fence element); compare draft/08-detailed-description.md, fence paragraph
findings.detail: The disclosure and the detailed description both recite that the fence is perpendicular to the rail. Both independent apparatus claims instead recite that the downwardly projecting portion is perpendicular to the rail. Claims and description must use the same relationship for the same feature; as drafted the claims assign the disclosed geometric relationship to a different element than the specification does.
findings.evidence: Candidate claim 1: "the fence having a downwardly projecting portion that extends below the lower face and that is perpendicular to the rail for bearing against the straight edge"; candidate claim 13: "the fixed fence having a downwardly projecting portion that extends below the lower face and that is perpendicular to the rail for bearing against the straight edge". Description: "The fence 30 is perpendicular to the rail 10, so that when the downwardly projecting portion 32 is held against the workpiece edge 92 the rail 10 extends inward across the front face of the workpiece 90." Source: "The fence is perpendicular to the rail, so the rail extends inward across the workpiece when the fence bears against the edge."
findings.fix: In claim 1 amend to: "a fence releasably secured to the first end of the rail by two screws received in two corresponding mounting holes, the fence being perpendicular to the rail and having a downwardly projecting portion that extends below the lower face for bearing against the straight edge, ...". In claim 13 amend correspondingly to: "a fixed fence at the first end of the rail, the fixed fence being perpendicular to the rail and having a downwardly projecting portion that extends below the lower face for bearing against the straight edge, so that the rail extends inward across the front face;".

findings.title: Claim 11 recites that every setting is read from the distance marks, contradicting the description
findings.where: draft/09-claims.md, claim 11; compare draft/08-detailed-description.md, penultimate substantive paragraph
findings.detail: Claim 11 states that every setting of the jig is read directly from the distance marks. The description states that settings are read from three separate features, and the specification elsewhere makes clear that the centerline placement is set by sighting the transverse center index and the sight notch, not by reading the distance marks. The claim as drafted is inconsistent with the description, and the center index and sight notch cannot simply be added to claim 11 because claim 1 does not recite them (no antecedent basis).
findings.evidence: Candidate claim 11: "...and every setting of the drilling jig is made mechanically and read directly from the distance marks." Description: "Every setting is made mechanically and is read directly from the distance marks 18, the transverse center index 24, and the sight notch 26." Source: "The tool has no motor, battery, electronic sensor, or network connection."
findings.fix: Amend claim 11 to read: "11. The drilling jig of claim 1, wherein the drilling jig has no motor, no battery, no electronic sensor, and no network connection, and every setting of the drilling jig is made mechanically." (Delete "and read directly from the distance marks".)

findings.title: Claim 13 locates the transverse center index "on the upper face", a position not in the source or the description
findings.detail: Claim 13 adds a positional limitation placing the transverse center index on the upper face of the rail. The disclosure says only that the rail has the index at its midpoint, and the detailed description likewise says only that the rail has it at its midpoint and that it runs across the rail. Claim 4, reciting the same feature, correctly omits the face. The added location is therefore both untraced and inconsistent with the parallel claim and the description.
findings.evidence: Candidate claim 13: "a transverse center index on the upper face at a midpoint of the rail". Claim 4 (same feature): "wherein the rail has a transverse center index at a midpoint of the rail." Description: "the rail 10 has a transverse center index 24 at its midpoint. The transverse center index 24 is a mark that runs across the rail 10 transverse to the length of the rail 10..." Nearest source: "The rail has a transverse center index at its midpoint." No source passage assigns the index to a particular face.
findings.fix: Amend claim 13 to read: "a transverse center index at a midpoint of the rail, and a shallow V-shaped sight notch formed in the second end of the rail and aligned with the transverse center index, for sighting on the centerline;". (Delete "on the upper face".) Leave FIG-7.md unchanged, since a top plan view necessarily shows the mark on the visible surface and that placement is not verbalized as a relationship in the application text.

findings.title: Numeral 32 is cross-referenced to FIG. 1 and relied on in the FIG. 6 paragraph but is absent from both figure briefs
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md (fence paragraph and FIG. 6 paragraph); figures/FIG-1.md and figures/FIG-6.md numeral lists
findings.detail: The description cites FIG. 1 for the downwardly projecting portion 32 and then, expressly "Referring to FIG. 6", describes which longitudinal side of the rail portion 32 lies on in the first and second fence orientations. Neither FIG-1.md nor FIG-6.md depicts or lists numeral 32, so the text refers the reader to views that do not carry the part it discusses. The part itself is fully supported by the disclosure, so the inconsistency is corrected by labeling it, not by deleting matter.
findings.evidence: Description: "The fence 30 includes a downwardly projecting portion 32 that extends below the lower face 14 and bears against the workpiece edge 92 (see FIG. 1)." and "Referring to FIG. 6, ... In a first orientation, the downwardly projecting portion 32 lies on a first longitudinal side of the rail 10." FIG-1.md numeral list: "10, 30, 50, 58, 62, 70, 90, 92" (no 32), although the brief already shows the fence "hangs down, contacting a workpiece edge 92". FIG-6.md numeral list: "10, 30, 34, 36" (no 32). Source support for the part: "The fence extends downward from the lower face and bears against one straight edge of the workpiece" and "...moves the downwardly projecting part of the fence from one longitudinal side of the rail to the opposite longitudinal side."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-1.md, change "A fence 30 is attached to the left end of the rail 10 and hangs down, contacting a workpiece edge 92" to "A fence 30 is attached to the left end of the rail 10 and has a downwardly projecting portion 32 that extends below the rail 10 and contacts a workpiece edge 92", and add "- 32: downwardly projecting portion" to its numeral list. In figures/FIG-6.md, add the sentence "The fence 30 has a downwardly projecting portion 32 that stands on one longitudinal side of the rail 10." and add "- 32: downwardly projecting portion" to its numeral list.

findings.title: FIG. 1 depicts an unidentified round body on the second guide carriage that is the disclosed clamp knob 78
findings.where: figures/FIG-1.md, second paragraph and numeral list
findings.detail: The brief instructs that a round body of like size stand on the second guide carriage but leaves it unnamed and unnumbered, while the identical element on the first carriage is called out as clamp knob 58. The element is the second carriage's clamp knob, which the disclosure affirmatively provides and which the numeral ledger already assigns numeral 78. An unexplained element in a figure is an avoidable drawing objection and an internal inconsistency with FIG. 3, which labels the same part 78.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-1.md): "The first guide carriage 50 has a clamp knob 58 on top, shown schematically as a plain round body. A round body of like size stands on top of the second guide carriage 70." Numeral ledger: "78 | clamp knob of the second guide carriage". Source: "Each carriage has a threaded clamp knob above the rail."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-1.md, change the second sentence to "A clamp knob 78 of like size stands on top of the second guide carriage 70, shown schematically as a plain round body." and add "- 78: clamp knob of the second guide carriage" to the numeral list for FIG. 1.

findings.title: Description asserts a bushing wear mechanism (bore enlarged by use) that the source does not disclose
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph beginning "The drill bushing 54 and the drill bushing 74 are wear parts."
findings.detail: The disclosure states that the drill bushings are replaceable wear parts made from hardened metal. It does not state how they wear. The candidate specifies bore enlargement as the wear condition that prompts replacement, which is an untraced operating condition supplied from common engineering knowledge rather than from the inventor.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "Each is made of hardened metal and is received in the body of its guide carriage as a separate piece, so that a drill bushing whose bore has been enlarged by use can be withdrawn from the guide carriage and replaced." Nearest source: "The drill bushings are replaceable wear parts and are made from hardened metal." No source passage describes bore enlargement or any other wear mode.
findings.fix: Amend the sentence to: "Each is made of hardened metal and is received in the body of its guide carriage as a separate piece, so that a worn drill bushing can be withdrawn from the guide carriage and replaced." No claim amendment is needed, since claims 9 and 17 already recite only hardened metal, separability, withdrawability, and replaceability.
